cards.front: carbohydrate
cards.back: A nutrient that gives your body energy. Rice, bread and potatoes are rich in it.
cards.say: carbohydrate. A nutrient that gives your body energy. Rice, bread and potatoes are rich in it.

cards.front: protein
cards.back: A nutrient that helps your body grow and repair. Fish, eggs, beans and tofu have lots.
cards.say: protein. A nutrient that helps your body grow and repair. Fish, eggs, beans and tofu have lots.

cards.front: fat
cards.back: A nutrient that gives energy and keeps the body warm. Oil and butter have lots.
cards.say: fat. A nutrient that gives energy and keeps the body warm. Oil and butter have lots.

cards.front: vitamins and minerals
cards.back: Nutrients that help your body stay healthy. Fruit and vegetables have many.
cards.say: vitamins and minerals. Nutrients that help your body stay healthy. Fruit and vegetables have many.

cards.front: fibre
cards.back: A part of plant foods that helps food move through the body. Whole grains and vegetables have fibre.
cards.say: fibre. A part of plant foods that helps food move through the body. Whole grains and vegetables have fibre.

cards.front: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
cards.back: Carbohydrates, such as rice, noodles and bread.
cards.say: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy? Carbohydrates, such as rice, noodles and bread.

cards.front: Which nutrient helps your body grow and repair?
cards.back: Protein, such as eggs, fish and beans.
cards.say: Which nutrient helps your body grow and repair? Protein, such as eggs, fish and beans.

cards.front: Which food group is rice in?
cards.back: Carbohydrates.
cards.say: Which food group is rice in? Carbohydrates.

cards.front: Which food group is chicken in?
cards.back: Protein.
cards.say: Which food group is chicken in? Protein.

cards.front: Which food group is milk in?
cards.back: Dairy, which gives calcium for strong bones and teeth.
cards.say: Which food group is milk in? Dairy, which gives calcium for strong bones and teeth.

cards.front: Which food group is an orange in?
cards.back: Fruit, which gives vitamins.
cards.say: Which food group is an orange in? Fruit, which gives vitamins.

cards.front: Which food group is spinach in?
cards.back: Vegetables, which give vitamins and fibre.
cards.say: Which food group is spinach in? Vegetables, which give vitamins and fibre.

cards.front: Which food group is butter mostly in?
cards.back: Fats.
cards.say: Which food group is butter mostly in? Fats.

cards.front: Why do we need water?
cards.back: Water helps the body work and carries nutrients around. We need to drink often.
cards.say: Why do we need water? Water helps the body work and carries nutrients around. We need to drink often.

cards.front: balanced diet
cards.back: Eating the right amount of each food group.
cards.say: balanced diet. Eating the right amount of each food group.

cards.front: Which should we eat more of, vegetables or sweets?
cards.back: Vegetables. Sweets should be only a small treat.
cards.say: Which should we eat more of, vegetables or sweets? Vegetables. Sweets should be only a small treat.

cards.front: Which nutrient helps repair a cut or muscle?
cards.back: Protein.
cards.say: Which nutrient helps repair a cut or muscle? Protein.

cards.front: Why is breakfast important?
cards.back: It gives you energy for the morning.
cards.say: Why is breakfast important? It gives you energy for the morning.

cards.front: Why should we eat fruit and vegetables every day?
cards.back: They give vitamins, minerals and fibre to keep us well.
cards.say: Why should we eat fruit and vegetables every day? They give vitamins, minerals and fibre to keep us well.

cards.front: True or false: A balanced diet means eating only one food group.
cards.back: False. A balanced diet includes all the food groups.
cards.say: True or false: A balanced diet means eating only one food group. False. A balanced diet includes all the food groups.

cards.front: Name two sources of protein that come from plants.
cards.back: Beans and tofu. Nuts and lentils too.
cards.say: Name two sources of protein that come from plants. Beans and tofu. Nuts and lentils too.

cards.front: Which foods give calcium for strong bones?
cards.back: Milk, cheese or yoghurt.
cards.say: Which foods give calcium for strong bones? Milk, cheese or yoghurt.

cards.front: What can happen if someone eats too many sugary foods?
cards.back: They can get tooth decay and may become unhealthy.
cards.say: What can happen if someone eats too many sugary foods? They can get tooth decay and may become unhealthy.

cards.front: Which food group does bread belong to?
cards.back: Carbohydrates.
cards.say: Which food group does bread belong to? Carbohydrates.
